  = note: type is never used

W1003.title: Unused import
W1003.message: Imported module or symbol is never used
W1003.example: use std.json; // json is never used
W1003.error_output:
warning[W1003]: Unused import: 'json'
 --> example.yx:1:1
  |
1 | use std.json;
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = note: import is never used

W1004.title: Unused private variable
W1004.help: Variable is never referenced, consider removing or using the variable; pub variables are external interfaces and will not trigger this warning
W1004.error_output:
warning[W1004]: Unused variable: 'dead_var'
 --> example.yx:1:1
  |
1 | dead_var = 42
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = note: variable is never used

W1005.title: Unused private method
W1005.help: Method has never been referenced, consider removing it or adding a call; pub methods are external interfaces and will not trigger this warning
W1005.error_output:
warning[W1005]: Unused method: 'dead_method'
 --> example.yx:1:1
  |
1 | fn Foo.dead_method() { }
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = note: Method was never used

E2014.title: Use of moved value
E2014.template: '{name}' has been moved and cannot be used again
E2014.help: The value has been moved to a new owner. To use it again, use a reference or clone it.

E2016.title: Immutable assignment
E2016.help: Declare the variable with `mut` to allow assignment.

E2018.title: Mutable/immutable borrow conflict
E2018.help: Ensure no immutable references exist before creating a mutable reference.

E2019.title: Double free
E2019.help: Ensure the value is freed only once.

E2020.title: Use after free
E2020.help: Use the value before it is freed, or refactor the code.

E2027.title: unsafe dereference
E2027.template: Cannot dereference a raw pointer outside an `unsafe` block
E2027.help: Wrap the dereference operation in an `unsafe` block.

E3022.title: Entry main signature mismatch
E3022.template: Entry '{name}' signature mismatch: invoked with zero arguments at runtime, but it requires '{expected}', found '{found}'
E3022.help: The program entry is always called with no arguments. Please write main as a no-argument form `main: () -> Void = { ... }`; if external input is needed, use argv/environment variables from std.os.

E3023.title: Top-level executable statements are not allowed
E3023.message: In the Bin role, the program body is main; the top level can only contain declarations
E3023.template: In the Bin role (when yaoxiang.toml exists), top-level executable statements are not allowed — the program body is main
E3023.help: Move this statement into the main function body; if you really want top-level statements to serve as the program body, remove yaoxiang.toml and use Script mode (without a manifest, top-level statements are executed in written order).

E1103.title: Brackets are not allowed in type position
E1103.message: Type arguments use parentheses; brackets are value-level indexing
E1103.template: '{name}[...]' is not type syntax — type arguments must use parentheses
E1103.help: Write it as `{name}(...)`. Brackets are **value-level** indexing (`list[0]`); in type position you can only use parentheses: `List(Int)`, not `List[Int]`.

E3004.title: Unsupported iterator
E3004.help: Currently, only range and list iterators are supported.

E3005.title: IR generation error
E3005.help: This is an internal error; please report this issue.

E3006.title: Unresolved variable
E3006.template: Internal IR generation error: variable '{name}' could not be resolved
E3006.help: A variable reference remains unresolved at the IR generation stage, indicating that the type checker missed it. This is a compiler internal consistency issue; please report it.

E3007.title: Top-level binding initializer must be a constant
E3007.template: The initializer of top-level binding '{name}' must be a compile-time constant expression
E3007.help: Top-level bindings are compile-time constants (the accessor function directly returns a folded value) and do not support runtime-computed initializers. Please change the computation to a literal/constant expression, or move it into a function body.

E3014.title: Register overflow
E3014.help: Reduce the number of local variables or simplify expressions.

E3019.title: Circular dependency in top-level bindings
E3019.template: Initialization of top-level bindings forms a circular dependency: {cycle}
E3019.help: Break the cycle: change the initialization of one of the bindings so that it does not reference other bindings in the cycle, or use a function to defer evaluation.

E3020.title: Missing program entry
E3020.template: Executable is missing the main function ({path})
E3020.help: Define an entry: main = { ... }. When main is absent in Bin role, all functions are unreachable.

E3021.title: Entry is not a function
E3021.template: Program entry '{name}' must be a function, but it is a value binding
E3021.help: The entry must be callable: write it as main = { ... } or main: () -> Void = { ... }; value bindings (such as main: Int = 5) will not be executed.

E4010.title: Constant division by zero
E4010.help: Ensure that the divisor in the constant expression is not zero.

E4011.title: Constant overflow
E4011.help: The result of the constant expression is out of the type's range.

E4012.title: Constant recursion too deep
E4012.template: Constant evaluation exceeded maximum recursion depth {limit}
E4012.help: Simplify the constant expression to reduce recursion.

E4014.title: Constant evaluation failed
E4014.help: Ensure the expression can be evaluated at compile-time.

E4018.title: Refinement predicate violated
E4018.help: The predicate was falsified — there exists an assignment that makes the constraint false. Please check variable values or relax the constraint.

E4019.title: Type equality does not hold
E4019.message: Type equality was falsified within the proof pipeline
E4019.template: Type equality does not hold: expected {expected}, found {found}
E4019.help: Check the type computation of the components or provide a proof function.

E5006.title: Duplicate import
E5006.template: Duplicate import: '{name}' has already been imported

E5007.title: Module exports
E5007.help: Available exports are listed in the error message

E6006.title: Function not found (runtime)
E6006.help: Ensure the function is defined and spelled correctly

E6007.title: Runtime error
E6007.help: Check the error message for details

E0016.title: Expected expression
E0016.help: Provide a valid expression at this position
E0016.error_output:
error[E0016]: expected expression
 --> example.yx:1:5
  |
1 | x = ;
  |     ^ expected expression after '='

E0018.title: Keyword as name
E0018.message: Keywords cannot be used as variable or expression names
E0018.template: '{keyword}' is a keyword and cannot be used as a name
E0018.help: Use a different identifier instead of the keyword
E0018.error_output:
error[E0018]: keyword used as name
 --> example.yx:1:1
  |
1 | if = 1;
  | ^^ 'if' is a keyword

E1092.title: Invalid refinement type argument form
E1092.message: Refinement type argument cannot be converted to a compile-time constant expression
E1092.template: '{name}' requires a compile-time constant argument, but the given argument cannot be converted
E1092.help: Predicate/proof function arguments must be literals, variables, or single-argument type applications; otherwise refinement constraints cannot be generated
E1092.error_output: error[E1092]: 'IsSmall' requires a compile-time constant argument, but the given argument cannot be converted

E1093.title: Refinement argument count mismatch
E1093.help: The argument count must match the predicate declaration; otherwise refinement constraints cannot be generated

E1094.title: Unused compile-time value parameter
E1094.message: Compile-time value parameter is not referenced in the type body
E1094.template: '{param}' is declared as a compile-time value parameter of '{type}', but is not referenced in the type body
E1094.help: Reference the parameter in a type position (field type, inner Fn parameter type, Assert/Array type argument), or remove it from the declaration
E1094.example: Foo: (T: Type, N: Int) -> Type = { x: T }
E1094.error_output: error[E1094]: 'N' is declared as a compile-time value parameter of 'Foo', but is not referenced in the type body

E1095.title: Unknown interface
E1095.template: Unknown interface: '{name}' (the name referenced by the type body is not a registered type constructor)
E1095.help: Check the name spelling, or first declare the interface with `Iface: (Self: Type) -> Type = {{ ... }}`

E1096.title: Interface parameter count mismatch
E1096.help: Provide arguments according to the number of type parameters declared by the interface

E1097.title: Interface member name conflict
E1097.template: Member '{member}' of type '{type}' conflicts with an interface member (fields and methods share a namespace, §1.2)
E1097.help: Rename the field or interface member

E1098.title: Interface method not implemented
E1098.template: Type '{type}' does not implement method '{method}' of interface '{interface}'
E1098.help: Declare the method with `Type.method: Signature = ...`, or provide a binding in the type body

E1099.title: Interface method signature mismatch
E1099.template: Method '{method}' of type '{type}' does not match the interface signature: expected {expected}, found {found}
E1099.help: Make the implementation signature exactly match the interface member signature (§3 prohibits overriding, allows overloading)

E1100.title: Duplicate interface method implementation
E1100.template: Method '{method}' of type '{type}' is implemented multiple times (same-signature override is forbidden, §3)
E1100.help: Remove the duplicate implementations and keep only one

E1101.title: Type does not implement interface
E1101.template: Type '{type}' does not implement interface '{interface}' and cannot enter that existential type position
E1101.help: Implement all members of the interface and instantiate it within the type body (e.g., `Animal(Dog)`); for RFC-011b scenarios (equality/operators), implement the corresponding interface for the type, and linear token fields must be removed first

E1102.title: Loop control statement outside of loop
E1102.message: break/continue can only be used inside while/for loop bodies
E1102.help: Move '{keyword}' inside a while/for loop body

E1064.title: Invalid binding position index
E1064.template: Invalid binding position index: {positions} (function has {total} parameters in total)
E1064.help: Binding positions must fall within the parameter range of the bound function (out of bounds or still negative after normalization). Please check the position numbers of the method binding.

E4020.title: Proof function required
E4020.message: Constraint cannot be proved at compile-time; a proof function is required
E4020.template: A proof function is required to verify the constraint
E4020.help: Add a proof function or provide a runtime check

E4021.title: Loop termination cannot be automatically proved
E4021.message: The compiler cannot synthesize a decreasing measure for this loop and cannot automatically prove its termination
E4021.template: Unable to automatically prove loop termination: no valid decreasing measure found
E4021.help: This is the coverage boundary of the compiler's automatic reasoning, not a program error. Please use a loop form with an explicit decreasing variable (e.g., a counter variable with a lower bound that decreases each iteration), or refer to RFC-027 §7 for the measure strategy and coverage.

W1080.title: Compile-time proof degraded
W1080.message: The constraint cannot be proven at compile-time, and has been degraded to a runtime check
W1080.template: Unable to prove constraint at compile-time, degraded to runtime check
W1080.help: Consider adding a proof function to improve safety

E6009.title: Invalid Range step
E6009.message: The Range step must be non-zero
E6009.help: iter/contains requires the dynamic step to be non-zero; please check the step expression

E6010.title: Integer parsing failed
E6010.message: The string cannot be parsed as an integer
E6010.help: Check whether the string is a valid integer (may contain a sign)

E6011.title: Floating-point parsing failed
E6011.message: The string cannot be parsed as a floating-point number
E6011.help: Check whether the string is a valid floating-point number

E2029.title: Reference cycle in spawn
E2029.message: Reference cycle detected in spawn block
E2029.help: References captured by spawn cannot form cyclic dependencies; please check the capture list

E3008.title: Unsupported match pattern
E3008.template: match pattern '{pattern}' is not yet implemented: currently only literal and wildcard (_) patterns are supported
E3008.help: Variant destructuring (ok(v)/err(e)/some(x)), struct, tuple, or pattern-with-guard are not yet implemented (planned in RFC-010b); the previous implementation silently mis-translated these, and is now rejected at compile-time. For handling Result, please use the `?` operator instead.

E3018.title: Monomorphization instantiation failure
E3018.help: The monomorphizer could not generate a specialized version for the given type arguments (a common cause is a mismatch between the number of type arguments and the number of generic parameters). Previously, this error was silently skipped, only surfacing at runtime as a "missing function table" error.

E2030.title: Refinement type constraint violated
E2030.template: After assigning to '{assigned}', '{var}' no longer satisfies the refinement type constraint: {constraint} (counterexample: {counterexample})
E2030.help: Refinement type annotations require the dependent variable to still satisfy the predicate constraint after the relevant assignment. Please adjust the assignment to make the constraint hold, or relax the type annotation.

E1014.title: Unknown named argument name
E1014.message: The argument name used in the call is not in the function's parameter list
E1014.help: use a name from the parameter list, or pass arguments by position
E1014.error_output:
error[E1014]: unknown named argument name
 --> example.yx:1:1
  |
1 | add(b = 1, c = 2);
  |     ^ function 'add' has no parameter named 'c' (available: a, b)

E1015.title: Argument specified more than once
E1015.message: The same parameter is specified by both a positional and a named argument
E1015.template: parameter '{name}' of function '{func}' is specified more than once
E1015.help: each parameter can only be passed once: remove the extra named or positional argument
E1015.error_output:
error[E1015]: argument specified more than once
 --> example.yx:1:1
  |
1 | add(1, a = 2);
  |          ^ parameter 'a' of function 'add' is specified more than once

E1104.title: interface implementation not in the type's defining module
E1104.message: operator interface implementation must be written in the type's defining module
E1104.template: type '{type}' is not defined by this module; cannot implement interface '{interface}' for it in this module
E1104.help: Orphan rule: implementations follow the type's defining module. Interface instantiations can only be written for types defined in this module (e.g. `Add(Point, Point, Point)`); operator interfaces for builtin types (Int/List, etc.) are provided by the core and cannot be supplemented

E1105.title: variant constructor cannot be accessed as a field
E1105.message: variant constructors can only be used in the call form `Type.Variant(...)`
E1105.template: '{variant}' is a variant constructor of the sum type '{type}', not a data field
E1105.help: to construct a value, write `{type}.{variant}(...)`; to extract the payload from a sum type value, use match variant destructuring (RFC-010b). Record fields of a sum type are all promoted to variants; runtime values do not carry a field table

E1032.title: duplicate pattern binding
E1032.message: '{name}' is bound multiple times in the same pattern
E1032.template: duplicate pattern binding: '{name}' appears multiple times in the same pattern
E1032.help: each name can only be bound once in a pattern; to match two identical fields, use different names (same as Rust semantics)

E1033.title: inconsistent bindings in or-pattern
E1033.message: the name sets bound by each `|` alternative differ
E1033.template: inconsistent or-pattern bindings: both sides of `|` must bind the same name set
E1033.help: each alternative of an or-pattern `a(x) | b(x)` must introduce exactly the same binding names (same as Rust semantics)

E1034.title: struct pattern missing field
E1034.message: struct pattern does not cover field '{field}'
E1034.template: struct pattern missing field '{field}' (fields of '{struct}' must be fully covered)
E1034.help: struct patterns must list all fields; the `..` shorthand is not yet supported

E1106.title: Constraint not satisfied
E1106.template: Type '{type}' does not implement `{interface}` — the constraint `{param}: {interface}` on the generic parameter `{param}` does not hold at this call site
E1106.help: Implement the corresponding interface for this type (write an interface instantiation in the type body and define methods), or use an argument that already implements the interface

E1107.title: Method overload ambiguity
E1107.message: '{key}' has {count} candidate matches and cannot be resolved
E1107.template: Method overload ambiguity: '{key}' has {count} candidate matches that cannot be distinguished
E1107.help: Add a type annotation to the call result (e.g., `x: T = obj.m()`), or make the parameter types of the overload candidates distinguishable

E2031.title: Refinement constraint cannot be proven
E2031.template: After assigning to '{assigned}', the refinement type constraint of '{var}': {constraint} cannot be statically proven in the proof kernel
E2031.help: RFC-027 requires all refinement constraints to be proven at compile time — if they cannot be proven, it is a compile error. Please rewrite the constraint so that its arguments can be evaluated statically (literals or literal-foldable expressions), or provide a proof function returning Type to participate in compile-time execution.

E6012.title: Invalid code point
E6012.message: from_char_code received an invalid code point (negative, in the surrogate range, or beyond U+10FFFF)
E6012.help: Check that the code point is within U+0000..U+10FFFF and not in the surrogate range (U+D800..U+DFFF)
